newsitem.title: UK: Electricity supply shares fall on absence of bids.
newsitem.headline: Electricity supply shares fall on absence of bids.

text.p: Shares in the few remaining independent UK electricity supply companies moved lower in mid-morning trading on Thursday as further takeover bids failed to materialise, traders said.

Shares in bid favourite East Midlands Electricity Plc were down 9 1/2 pence to 534 by 1051 GMT, while London Electricity Plc slipped 13 pence to 595 and Yorkshire Electricty Plc was down 8 1/2 at 729.
Some switching helped to boost generators, with National Power Plc up 7 pence at 399 1/2 and PowerGen up 8 1/2 at 499.

SG Strauss Turnbull analyst Marshall Whiting said the figures for water companies were "fairly sensible." But he said the numbers on electricity "are too high. I think we are talking about 1.5 billion stg to 2.0 billion stg from the electricity companies."
Greig Middleton analyst David Campbell said that any windfall tax would be "arbitrary and unjustified" and added that attempts to estimate it were "irresponsible."
"We don't really have any good solid basis on which to assess the overall scale of the tax or how they will assess it on individual companies," he said.
Campbell added that indications from within the Labour Party about the levy had been contradictory. "We are hearing widely different stories about it," he said.
Shares in BAA Plc were down 10 pence to 499 by 1106 GMT, recovering from a low of 483 pence after the FT calculated it could face an extra tax bill of more than 500 million stg under Labour's plans.
BAA said it was not an appropriate target for a windfall tax and rejected the basis of the FT's estimates.
